messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=db-primary latency high, multiple 502s reported, auto-pager to @oncall-sre (PD: P12345). check runbook: /runbooks/db-conn-surge
Maya K: acked via PD, landing here. seeing a bunch of `pg` connection errors in the logs, 500s to customers, noise on redis too?
Ravi S: I see redis accept-queue spikes and pgbouncer max_client hits around the same time. stack traces show backend pool exhaustion.
Tom B: Confirming. Metrics: DB max_connections ~98/100, pgbouncer waiting clients ~850, redis instantaneous clients ~12000 (limit 15000). Latency -> p50 120ms -> p99 3.4s.
Maya K: Customer impact: support dashboard shows ~2% of web requests returning 502/timeout between 06:12-06:23 UTC. A few enterprise customers reported errors. We should mark incident priority P1 until stabilized.
Desk SRE: quick mitigation idea: enable readonly fallback for low-risk paths to reduce write pressure, and temporarily increase pgbouncer pool size on the replicas. Anyone on warm-up for infra changes?
Ravi S: running a small config bump on pgbouncer now (thread_pool + 20). Will monitor. If we hit DB file descriptor limit, revert.
Tom B: Also toggling cache bypass for heavy write jobs: setting feature flag `disable-job-writes` for the ingestion pipeline (short-lived).
Maya K: Commands:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/ingest-worker DISABLE_JOB_WRITES=true
ssh db-primary -- sudo systemctl reload pgbouncer
```
I'll run the first one after approvals.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: alert escalated to team lead because initial ack but no mitigate recorded within 5m. PD notes: escalation path triggered.
Support Team: we emailed affected customers with a brief note. keeping churn low.
Ravi S: pgbouncer bump applied on replica pool nodes (3/4). observing backlog drop from 850 -> 320 waiters, pg connections stable at 102. redis clients still high but not exceeding max.
Tom B: Starting a rolling restart of the ingest-worker replicas with stagger 30s to allow conn drain. This should reduce concurrent DB write bursts.
Maya K: Observation: KV cache TTLs are getting invalidated due to a job storm; I'm re-enabling prefix caching temporarily to reduce upstream hits.
Desk SRE: quick check: are there any long-running transactions holding connections? `SELECT pid, age(now(), query_start), state, query FROM pg_stat_activity` showed a handful > 2m. Killing top offenders.
Ravi S: Killed 4 long-running transactions; p99 latency dropped to 900ms. Good sign.
Tom B: Rolling restarts complete on all ingest workers. No new 502 spikes for 6m.
Maya K: Can someone run a synthetic customer flow to validate end-to-end? @Support Team please confirm a few sample accounts.
Support Team: ran smoke for three accounts, all green. No further 502s in the last 10m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: all alerts auto-resolved for P12345 (no active triggers).
Maya K: Summary for postmortem notes: root cause appears to be a burst of background ingestion jobs that concurrently opened DB connections and invalidated caches, causing pgbouncer wait pileup and cascading redis pressure. Mitigations performed: pgbouncer connection bump, killed long tx, rolled ingest workers, toggled disable_job_writes flag, re-enabled prefix caching, customer comms.
Tom B: Action items:
- add admission rate-limit to ingestion pipeline (Ravi)
- add auto-splay for pgbouncer scaling instead of a single bump (Infra)
- add runbook step for quick readonly fallback + feature-flag command (Maya)
- add monitoring alert for long-running tx > 30s (Tom)
Maya K: handing off to post-incident review. if anything flares up ping PagerDuty again. closing channel in ~30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
